items.title: Anthropic's Claude models co-author a claimed proof of unforced Navier-Stokes blowup
items.summary: Mathematicians Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) posted a 79-page paper on November 20 claiming the first proof of finite-time blowup for the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with no artificial external forcing, a cleaner version of the open Millennium Prize problem than OpenAI's forced-equation result from September. The authors say Anthropic's Claude models wrote large parts of the heavily LLM-assisted proof, building on their earlier forced-Euler and hypodissipative Navier-Stokes drafts, with a companion Lean formalization. Terence Tao reviewed the work on his blog, calling the proof strategy 'broadly clear' and the paper 'technically human-readable,' but said it still needs a properly written, professionally checked version; no independent expert has yet confirmed it's correct.
items.whyItMatters: Not a direct build input, but a vivid, well-scrutinized data point on how far Claude's models have come at generating long, rigorous technical writing — relevant if Romain's backend ever leans on Claude for more than conversation, like structured grammar explanations or exercise generation.
